extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on preparing a manuscript and submitting queries to find and obtain representation from a literary agent, including research, query-letter craft, submission protocol, and networking strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect Your Manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Before approaching literary agents, ensure your manuscript is in its best possible shape. Revise, edit, and polish your work until it shines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek multiple rounds of revision and polishing; agents look for polished, compelling stories that stand out from the crowd. Use the waiting and submission periods to continue improving your craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek feedback from critique partners or beta readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek feedback from critique partners or beta readers to gain valuable insights and make necessary improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external readers to identify weaknesses, blind spots, and opportunities to strengthen plot, character, pacing, and prose before querying; actionable feedback can raise a manuscript to agent-ready quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research literary agents who represent your genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the time to research literary agents who represent your genre or category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for agents with a track record of success in your niche and check their recent client list to see if your work aligns with their interests. Make sure the agent actively represents books like yours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate an agency's deal history and sales data
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking at a literary agency’s number of deals and amount of money for deals is a valuable resource for finding literary agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an agent's deal history and sale amounts as indicators of effectiveness and market reach. Consider recent deals and the kinds of publishers they work with to judge fit and capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalize your query letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft a well-written and personalized query letter that showcases your book's unique selling points and aligns with the agent's preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the agent by name and mention why you specifically chose to query them. Keep the query concise, engaging, and free of errors — it's your first chance to make a strong impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit exactly what agents request (follow submission guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow submission guidelines to the letter. Submit the materials they request, typically including a query letter, a synopsis, and a sample of your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignoring guidelines can lead to automatic rejection. Check each agent's page for specific requirements (file types, subject lines, sample lengths) and tailor your submission accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be patient and persistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting a literary agent takes time. Expect to wait several weeks or even months for responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use waiting periods productively (improve writing, start new projects). Treat rejections as part of the process and stay positive; persistence and perseverance are key attributes to success in querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch and network at writing conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend writing conferences and industry events to meet literary agents in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Face-to-face pitching can leave a lasting impression and may result in requests for full manuscripts. Conferences also provide networking opportunities and industry insights that can improve chances of representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use social media professionally to connect with agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilize social media platforms like Twitter to connect with literary agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many agents share submission tips and manuscript wishlists on social media. Engage thoughtfully and maintain a professional tone — social media interaction can supplement but not replace formal querying.
